summary: date returns an ISO calendar-date string after applying modifiers from left to right.
documentation: date returns an ISO calendar-date string after applying modifiers from left to right. Adding a fixed number of days can cross month, year and leap-day boundaries without manually changing the day-of-month field.
inputs: tasks(id INTEGER, opened TEXT), with valid YYYY-MM-DD dates or NULL.
returns: id and follow_up, ordered by id.
caution: A fixed day offset is different from adding a calendar month. This task uses explicit dates and no now or localtime dependency.
scenarios: Generate a seven-day follow-up date from an opening date.
Compute a fixed return deadline in a local report.
Shift a dated checklist reminder across a month boundary.
title: Schedule a seven-day follow-up
problem: Return id and date(opened,'+7 days') AS follow_up from tasks, ordered by id. NULL opened dates stay NULL.
hint: Use a day modifier rather than adding seven to a text value.
goal: Use date() with day modifiers or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
